slot.brief: Use the identity a×(b×c) = (a·c)b − (a·b)c to compute a vector expression for given simple vectors; ask for the resulting vector or its magnitude.

stem: The position vectors of $P,Q,R,S$ are $(1,1,0),(3,2,-1),(2,4,2),(3,0,1)$, respectively. Find $|\vec{PQ}\times(\vec{PR}\times\vec{PS})|$.

verdicts.working: Let a=PQ=(2,1,-1), b=PR=(1,3,2), c=PS=(2,-1,1). Using a×(b×c)=b(a·c)-c(a·b), with a·c=2 and a·b=3, gives (-4,9,1). Its magnitude is √98=7√2.

working:
$\vec{PQ}=(2,1,-1),\quad \vec{PR}=(1,3,2),\quad \vec{PS}=(2,-1,1)$
$\vec{PQ}\cdot\vec{PS}=2,\quad \vec{PQ}\cdot\vec{PR}=3$
$\vec{PQ}\times(\vec{PR}\times\vec{PS})=2\vec{PR}-3\vec{PS}=(-4,9,1)$
$|(-4,9,1)|=\sqrt{16+81+1}=7\sqrt{2}$

Independent check: Let a=PQ=(2,1,-1), b=PR=(1,3,2), c=PS=(2,-1,1). Using a×(b×c)=b(a·c)-c(a·b), with a·c=2 and a·b=3, gives (-4,9,1). Its magnitude is √98=7√2.
solution:
Using $\vec a\times(\vec b\times\vec c)=\vec b(\vec a\cdot\vec c)-\vec c(\vec a\cdot\vec b)$, with $\vec a=\vec{PQ}=(2,1,-1)$, $\vec b=\vec{PR}=(1,3,2)$ and $\vec c=\vec{PS}=(2,-1,1)$:
$$\vec{PQ}\times(\vec{PR}\times\vec{PS})=2\vec{PR}-3\vec{PS}=(-4,9,1).$$
Hence, $|(-4,9,1)|=\sqrt{16+81+1}=7\sqrt{2}$.
